questions.title: Box class with three constructors (volumes)
questions.statement:
Isha owns a gift shop and packs gifts in boxes of three kinds. The program has a class Box with a length, a width, and a height. A box created without any details is a cube of side 1. A box created with one value is a cube whose side is that value. A box created with three values has the given length, width, and height. The function volume returns the volume of a box.
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
Formula used: Volume = length * width * height
questions.inputFormat: The first line of input consists of four space-separated doubles side, a, b, and c. The value side represents the side of the cube, and the values a, b, and c represent the length, the width, and the height of the third box.
questions.outputFormat: Line 1 prints "Default Box Volume: " followed by the volume of the box created without any details, rounded to two decimal places. Line 2 prints "Cube Volume: " followed by the volume of the cube created with the given side, rounded to two decimal places. Line 3 prints "Box Volume: " followed by the volume of the box created with the given length, width and height, rounded to two decimal places.
questions.easy: Create three Box objects in three different ways (no argument, one argument, three arguments), then print each object's volume with exactly two decimal places.
logic: Read the four double values.
Build Box first; (default constructor) -> volume 1.
Build Box second(side); -> all sides equal to side.
Build Box third(a, b, c); -> the given length, width, height.
Print each volume with fixed setprecision(2) and the exact labels.
algorithm: Define class Box with private doubles l, w, h.
Write Box() setting l = w = h = 1.
Write Box(double side) setting all three to side.
Write Box(double a, double b, double c) copying the three values.
Write double volume() returning l*w*h.
In main, read side, a, b, c; create the three objects; print with cout << fixed << setprecision(2).
mistakes: Constructor with same name but no return type - writing void Box() makes it NOT a constructor.
Using cout << volume without fixed << setprecision(2) gives the wrong decimals (e.g., 1.728 instead of 1.73).
Forgetting setprecision applies only after cout << fixed is set once before all prints.
questions.bugLabel: Output is printed without fixed << setprecision(2), so volumes show the wrong number of decimals.

questions.title: Document copy constructor and destructor order
questions.statement:
Sunita manages a digital library. The program has a class Document with a title and a number of pages. When a document is created with a title and the number of pages, the message "Created: " followed by the title is printed. When a document is created as a copy of another document, the copy gets the same number of pages, and its title is the title of the original document followed by "_copy", and the message "Copied: " followed by the new title is printed. When a document is destroyed, the message "Destroyed: " followed by its title is printed.
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
questions.inputFormat: The first line of input consists of a string title and an integer pages separated by a space.
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Created: " + title. Line 2: "Copied: " + copy title. Line 3: "Title: " + original title + ", Pages: " + original pages. Line 4: same for the copy. Lines 5 and 6: "Destroyed: " for the copy first, then for the original (objects are destroyed in the reverse order of their creation).
questions.easy: Create one Document, copy it (the copy's title gets "_copy" appended), show both, and let the destructors print in reverse creation order.
logic: Read title and pages; create d1 -> prints Created.
Create d2 as a copy of d1 -> copy constructor appends _copy and prints Copied.
Call show() for d1 then d2.
When main ends, d2 is destroyed first, then d1 (reverse order).
algorithm: Write Document(string t, int p): store values, print "Created: " + t.
Write Document(Document &other): title = other.title + "_copy"; pages = other.pages; print "Copied: " + title.
Write show() printing "Title: <title>, Pages: <pages>".
Write ~Document() printing "Destroyed: " + title.
In main: read input, create d1, create d2 = d1, call d1.show(); d2.show(); and return - destructors run automatically.
mistakes: Forgetting that objects destroy in REVERSE order of creation - the copy's Destroyed line comes first.
Using pass-by-value in the copy constructor (Document(Document b)) does not compile.
Appending _copy to the original's title before copying pages - the copy must keep the same page count.
questions.bugLabel: The copy constructor forgets to copy the page count, so the copy shows the wrong number of pages.

questions.title: BankAccount deposit / withdraw / getBalance
questions.statement:
Mahesh works at a bank counter. The program has a class BankAccount that keeps the balance of an account. The function deposit adds the given amount to the balance. The function withdraw removes the given amount from the balance only when the amount is less than or equal to the balance, and returns the message "Withdrawal Successful". Otherwise, the balance is not changed, and the function returns the message "Insufficient Balance". The function getBalance returns the balance with its decimal part.
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
questions.inputFormat: The first line of input consists of three space-separated doubles initial, dep, and wd.
questions.outputFormat: Line 1 prints the message returned by the withdrawal ("Withdrawal Successful" or "Insufficient Balance"). Line 2 prints "Balance: " followed by the final balance rounded to two decimal places.
questions.easy: Deposit some money, then try to withdraw - if there is enough balance the money goes out and the program says success, otherwise the balance stays the same and the program says insufficient.
logic: Read initial, dep, wd; create the account with initial.
Deposit dep.
Try to withdraw wd: allowed only when wd <= balance.
Print the returned message, then the balance with two decimals.
algorithm: Class BankAccount stores a private double balance.
deposit(double amount) adds amount to balance.
withdraw(double amount): if amount <= balance, subtract and return "Withdrawal Successful"; otherwise return "Insufficient Balance" WITHOUT changing the balance.
getBalance() returns balance.
main: read values, create account, deposit, print withdraw's message, print fixed setprecision(2) balance.
mistakes: Changing the balance in the failed case - it must stay untouched.
Comparing with < instead of <=: withdrawing exactly the whole balance must SUCCEED (see test 99.5 0.5 100.0 -> Balance 0.00).
Printing the message with cout inside withdraw - the function must RETURN the message.
questions.bugLabel: withdraw compares with < instead of <=, so withdrawing exactly the whole balance is wrongly rejected.

questions.title: Student with this pointer and method chaining
questions.statement:
Teacher Revathi adds grace marks to the marks of a student. The program has a class Student with a name and the marks. The constructor takes the name and the marks as parameters, which have the same names as the data members of the class. The member function addBonus adds the given bonus to the marks and returns the same student object, so that more than one bonus can be added one after the other in a single statement, for example s.addBonus(5).addBonus(3). The member function display prints the name and the marks of the student.
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
Formula used: Final marks = marks + first bonus + second bonus
questions.inputFormat: One line: string name and three integers marks, b1, b2.
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Name: " + name. Line 2: "Marks: " + final marks.
questions.constraints: 1 <= length of name <= 20 (no spaces); 0 <= marks, b1, b2 <= 100; marks + b1 + b2 <= 100
questions.easy: Add two bonuses to a student's marks one after another in a single statement, using the this pointer to return the same object.
logic: The constructor parameters shadow the data members, so use this->name and this->marks.
addBonus adds the bonus and returns *this so the next .addBonus() call continues on the same object.
display prints the final name and marks.
algorithm: Student(string name, int marks): assign this->name = name; this->marks = marks;
Student& addBonus(int bonus): this->marks += bonus; return *this;
void display(): print "Name: " and "Marks: " lines.
main: read name marks b1 b2, create s, call s.addBonus(b1).addBonus(b2); then s.display();
mistakes: Returning void from addBonus breaks the chain s.addBonus(b1).addBonus(b2) - it must return Student& (a reference).
Forgetting the this-> prefix when parameter names match member names (the parameter wins without it!).
Returning a copy instead of a reference would add bonuses to a temporary object - marks would stay unchanged.
questions.bugLabel: The constructor assigns the parameters to themselves (this-> is missing), so the object stores nothing.

questions.title: Player with static highest score and top player
questions.statement:
Rohan conducts an online quiz and keeps a leaderboard. The program has a class Player with a name and a score. The class also keeps two values that are shared by all the players: the highest score so far, and the name of the player who has it. At the start, the highest score is 0 and the top player is "None". Whenever a player is created, the shared values are updated only if the score of the new player is strictly greater than the highest score so far, so if two players have the same highest score, the player who came first stays on the top. The static functions getHighest and getTopPlayer return the two shared values.
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
questions.inputFormat: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n pairs of a string name and an integer score.
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Top Player: " + name. Line 2: "Highest Score: " + score.
questions.constraints: 1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= length of name <= 20 (no spaces); 1 <= score <= 100
questions.easy: As each new player joins, remember the best score so far and who scored it. The first player to reach a score stays on top if someone later ties it.
logic: Declare static int highest and static string topPlayer in the class.
Define them outside the class: int Player::highest = 0; string Player::topPlayer = "None";
In the constructor, update only when score > highest (strictly greater).
Static functions return the shared values without needing any object.
algorithm: Create Player objects one by one while reading input.
Constructor: if (score > highest) { highest = score; topPlayer = name; }
After reading all players, print Player::getTopPlayer() and Player::getHighest().
mistakes: Using >= instead of > - a tie must NOT replace the earlier player (see Priya 60 Kiran 60 -> Priya).
Forgetting the outside-the-class definitions of the static members -> 'undefined reference' linker error.
Calling static functions through an object only - they can (and should) be called as Player::getHighest().
questions.bugLabel: A tie with >= replaces the earlier top player, but a tie must keep the FIRST player.

questions.title: Count primes in a range and find the largest (procedural style)
questions.statement: Dinesh is a mathematics teacher who prepares number puzzles for his students. A prime number is a number greater than 1 that has no divisors other than 1 and itself. For two given numbers, he wants to know how many prime numbers lie between them, including both the numbers, and which is the largest of those prime numbers. Write a program in the procedural style, using a separate function to check whether a number is prime, and print the count of the prime numbers and the largest prime number in the range. If there is no prime number in the range, print "None" for the largest prime number.
questions.inputFormat: One line: two space-separated integers a and b (the range ends, inclusive).
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Prime Count: " + count. Line 2: "Largest Prime: " + largest (or "None" if no prime exists).
questions.easy: Count how many prime numbers are between a and b (including both) and print the biggest one, or None if there are no primes at all.
logic: A prime is a number >= 2 that no smaller number (up to its square root) divides.
Check every number from a to b with a separate isPrime function.
Count the primes and remember the last (largest) one found.
If count is 0, print None instead of a number.
algorithm: bool isPrime(int x): if x < 2 return false; for i = 2..sqrt(x): if x % i == 0 return false; return true.
Read a and b; loop i from a to b.
If isPrime(i): count++ and largest = i.
Print "Prime Count: " + count.
If count == 0 print "Largest Prime: None", else print largest.
mistakes: Starting the divisor loop at 1 (every number divides by 1) or forgetting x < 2 is not prime (1 is NOT prime).
Testing divisors up to x instead of sqrt(x) - too slow for large ranges.
Printing 0 instead of None when no prime exists.

questions.title: TemperatureLog class with private array (highest / lowest / average)
questions.statement:
Ganesh works at a weather station that records the temperature several times a day. The readings must be kept private inside a log object, and they can be added and analysed only through the member functions of the log. Write a program that defines a class TemperatureLog with a private array of readings and a count of the readings, and with public member functions to add a reading, to get the highest reading, to get the lowest reading, and to get the average of the readings. Read the temperatures of a day, add them to the log one by one, and print the highest, the lowest, and the average temperature.
Formula used: Average = Sum of all readings / Number of readings
questions.inputFormat: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated doubles (temperatures in degrees Celsius).
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Highest: " (2 decimals). Line 2: "Lowest: " (2 decimals). Line 3: "Average: " (2 decimals).
questions.easy: Store all temperature readings privately inside a class object, then ask the object for the highest, lowest and average values.
logic: The array and count are private - main can only call addReading, getHighest, getLowest, getAverage.
Start best/least from the FIRST reading (not from 0) - temperatures can be negative (e.g., -8.0).
Average = sum / count using double division.
algorithm: Class with private double readings[10]; int count; constructor sets count = 0.
addReading(double t): readings[count++] = t.
getHighest(): best = readings[0]; loop from 1; return best.
getLowest(): same with <.
getAverage(): sum all; return sum / count.
main: read n, loop adding readings, print three lines with fixed setprecision(2).
mistakes: Starting best at 0 fails when ALL temperatures are negative (test with -5.0 -2.5 ... -8.0 gives Lowest: -8.00).
Integer division for the average (sum/count with int sum) loses the decimals.
Reading temperatures into a local array instead of into the private member - defeats encapsulation.

questions.title: Timer class: constructor prints, countdown, destructor
questions.statement: Pooja is a chef who uses a countdown timer for every dish she cooks. A timer has a label, which is the name of the dish, and a number of seconds. When a timer is created, the message "Timer Created: " followed by the label is printed. When the timer is started, it counts down from the number of seconds to 1, printing every number on a separate line, and then prints "Time Up". When the timer is destroyed at the end of the program, the message "Timer Destroyed: " followed by the label is printed. Write a program that defines a class Timer with a parameterized constructor, a function to start the countdown, and a destructor. The parameters of the constructor have the same names as the data members of the class, so the this pointer must be used. Read the label and the number of seconds, create the timer, and start it.
questions.inputFormat: One line: string label and integer seconds.
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Timer Created: " + label. Next lines: numbers seconds..1, one per line. Next line: "Time Up". Last line: "Timer Destroyed: " + label.
questions.easy: A small class that prints a message when created, counts down from seconds to 1, prints Time Up, and prints a message when destroyed at the end of main.
logic: Constructor prints "Timer Created: " immediately.
start() loops i from seconds down to 1 printing each, then prints "Time Up".
The destructor runs automatically when main ends and prints "Timer Destroyed: ".
Constructor parameters shadow members -> use this->label and this->seconds.
algorithm: Timer(string label, int seconds): this->label = label; this->seconds = seconds; print created message.
void start(): for (i = seconds; i >= 1; i--) cout << i << endl; then "Time Up".
~Timer(): print "Timer Destroyed: " + label.
main: read label and seconds, create Timer t(label, seconds), call t.start().
mistakes: Printing "Time Up" inside the loop - it must come after the loop, exactly once.
Looping from 1 to seconds (wrong direction) - the countdown must print seconds first.
Using different parameter names and forgetting this-> is fine ONLY if names differ; here names match, so this-> is required.

questions.title: Leap year and days in a month
questions.statement: Vimala is designing a wall calendar and has to print the number of days in a given month of a given year. For this, she needs to know whether the year is a leap year. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 400, or if it is divisible by 4 but not divisible by 100. In a leap year, February has 29 days, and in other years February has 28 days. The months April, June, September, and November have 30 days, and all the other months have 31 days. Write a program that reads a year and a month number, and prints whether the year is a leap year and the number of days in the given month.
questions.inputFormat: One line: two space-separated integers year and month (1 = January .. 12 = December).
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Leap Year: Yes" or "Leap Year: No". Line 2: "Days: " + number of days.
questions.easy: Decide if the year is a leap year, then print how many days the chosen month has.
logic: Leap rule with the century trap: divisible by 400 -> leap; else divisible by 100 -> NOT leap; else divisible by 4 -> leap.
February: 29 if leap else 28.
April(4), June(6), September(9), November(11): 30 days; all other months: 31.
algorithm: Read year and month.
bool leap = (year % 400 == 0) || (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0).
If month == 2: days = leap ? 29 : 28; else if month in {4,6,9,11}: days = 30; else days = 31.
Print "Leap Year: Yes/No" then "Days: " + days.
mistakes: Checking only year % 4 == 0 - 1900 is NOT a leap year (divisible by 100 but not 400), while 2000 IS (divisible by 400).
Swapping the 30-day and 31-day month lists.
Forgetting that the leap message must be printed even when the month is not February.

questions.title: Complex class with overloaded + and *
questions.statement:
Professor Naveen teaches signals and needs a small tool for complex numbers. The program has a class Complex with a real part and an imaginary part. The operator + adds two complex numbers, and the operator * multiplies two complex numbers. The function display prints a complex number in the form (real, imaginary).
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
Formulas used: (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i; (a + bi) * (c + di) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i
questions.inputFormat: One line: four integers a, b, c, d (real, imag of first; real, imag of second).
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Sum: " + (real, imag). Line 2: "Product: " + (real, imag).
questions.easy: Overload + and * inside a Complex class so two complex numbers can be added and multiplied just like normal numbers, then print both results.
logic: Addition adds the real parts together and the imaginary parts together.
Multiplication uses (ac - bd) for the real part and (ad + bc) for the imaginary part.
display prints "(" << real << ", " << imag << ")" - note the comma and spaces.
operator+ and operator* each return a new Complex object.
algorithm: class Complex with int real, imag and a constructor Complex(int r, int i).
Complex operator+(Complex other): return Complex(real + other.real, imag + other.imag);
Complex operator*(Complex other): return Complex(real*other.real - imag*other.imag, real*other.imag + imag*other.real);
void display(): print in the (real, imag) form.
main: read a, b, c, d; build first(a,b) and second(c,d); print Sum and Product.
mistakes: Swapping the operands of the subtraction (bd - ac) or forgetting that i*i = -1 (so it MINUS ac... precisely: real = ac - bd).
Returning void from the operators - they must return Complex so the result can be stored.
Wrong display format: the output needs exactly "(4, 6)" with a comma and a space.
questions.bugLabel: The operands of the subtraction in operator* are swapped: the real part must be ac - bd, not bd - ac.

questions.title: Device -> Phone -> SmartPhone multilevel inheritance
questions.statement:
Anand works in a mobile factory. The program has three classes in three levels: the class Device has a brand, the class Phone is derived from Device and adds the storage in GB, and the class SmartPhone is derived from Phone and adds the operating system. The brand and the storage must be accessible inside the derived classes, but not outside the classes. Every constructor prints a message when an object is created, and every destructor prints a message when an object is destroyed. The function show of the class SmartPhone prints the brand, the storage, and the operating system.
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
questions.inputFormat: One line: string brand, int storage, string os.
questions.outputFormat: Lines 1-3: "Device Created: " + brand, "Phone Created: " + storage, "SmartPhone Created: " + os. Line 4: "Brand: ... , Storage: ... , OS: ...". Lines 5-7: destructor messages in reverse order (SmartPhone, Phone, Device).
questions.constraints: 1 <= length of brand, os <= 20 (no spaces); 1 <= storage <= 2048
questions.easy: Three classes stacked in a chain. Creating a SmartPhone first builds the Device part, then the Phone part, then the SmartPhone part - and destruction happens exactly backwards.
logic: Device holds protected string brand; Phone adds protected int storage; SmartPhone adds string os.
Each constructor prints its own Created message AFTER calling its base constructor (base first!).
Destructors print in reverse: SmartPhone, Phone, Device.
show() reads brand and storage directly because they are protected.
algorithm: class Device: protected brand; Device(string b) prints "Device Created: "; ~Device() prints "Device Destroyed: ".
class Phone : public Device: Phone(string b, int s) : Device(b) { print "Phone Created: "; }
class SmartPhone : public Phone: SmartPhone(b, s, o) : Phone(b, s) { print "SmartPhone Created: "; }
show() prints Brand / Storage / OS on one line with ", " separators.
main: read input, create SmartPhone s(brand, storage, os), call s.show().
mistakes: Passing values to the base constructor in the member-initialiser list - Phone(b, s) : Device(b) is required, otherwise there is no Device() default constructor.
Printing the Created messages in the wrong order (derived first) - the base ALWAYS constructs first.
Making brand/storage private - derived classes could not use them; they must be protected.
questions.bugLabel: Phone does not pass the brand to the Device constructor, so the base prints and stores the wrong brand.

questions.title: Overloaded function larger (int / double / three ints)
questions.statement:
Kavitha is a shop owner who compares prices and quantities every day. The program has three functions with the same name larger. The first function takes two integers and returns the larger integer. The second function takes two doubles and returns the larger double. The third function takes three integers and returns the largest integer.
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
questions.inputFormat: Line 1: three integers a, b, c. Line 2: two doubles x, y.
questions.outputFormat: Line 1: "Larger of two integers: " + max(a, b). Line 2: "Larger of two doubles: " + max(x, y) (2 decimals). Line 3: "Largest of three integers: " + max(a, b, c).
questions.easy: Three functions all named larger, distinguished by their parameter lists: (int, int), (double, double) and (int, int, int). The compiler picks the right one automatically.
logic: larger(int, int) returns the bigger of the two integers.
larger(double, double) works the same way for doubles.
larger(int, int, int) keeps a running maximum of three values.
fixed << setprecision(2) affects only the double line; integers still print without decimals.
algorithm: int larger(int a, int b): return a > b ? a : b (written with if).
double larger(double a, double b): same pattern.
int larger(int a, int b, int c): m = a; if (b > m) m = b; if (c > m) m = c; return m.
main: read a b c, then x y; set cout << fixed << setprecision(2); print the three lines calling larger with matching arguments.
mistakes: Calling larger(x, y) where x, y are ints - that calls the INT version; the double values must be read as doubles.
Expecting integers to print as 35.00: with fixed setprecision, an int still prints as 35 (the format flag does not change int printing).
Wrong output labels - copy them exactly, word for word.
questions.bugLabel: The two double values are read into int variables, so the int overload is called and decimals are lost.

questions.title: Cinema booking with exception throwing
questions.statement:
Mukesh manages the online booking of a cinema hall. The program has a class Cinema that keeps the number of seats available. The function book reduces the number of available seats by the number of seats requested. algorithm: Initialise key[] = huge, inTree[] = false, key[0] = 0, total = 0.
Repeat n times: find the smallest-key unvisited u; inTree[u] = true; total += key[u];
for every v: if graph[u][v] > 0 and not inTree[v] and graph[u][v] < key[v] -> key[v] = graph[u][v].
Print "MST Weight: " + total.
mistakes: Picking the smallest edge GLOBALLY instead of edges leaving the tree (Prim grows from the tree).
Adding graph[u][v] instead of key[v] to the total.
Missing the inTree check when relaxing - tree vertices would get re-added.
questions.bugLabel: The pick step ignores the keys (u == -1 only), so Prim takes vertices in index order instead of by smallest key.

questions.title: Dijkstra shortest distances with INF output
questions.statement:
Dilip runs a courier service in a region with n towns numbered from 0 to n-1. Every road joins two towns, can be used in both directions, and has a length in kilometers. The program stores the roads in an adjacency matrix, where 0 means that there is no road. The function dijkstra finds the length of the shortest route from the starting town to every town, using Dijkstra's method, and the function printDistances prints the lengths, with "INF" for a town that cannot be reached from the starting town.
The given code has errors, and it does not produce the correct output. Debug the code so that it works as described.
questions.inputFormat: Line 1: integers n and m. Next m lines: u, v, w. Last line: source.
questions.outputFormat: "Distances:" followed by " value" for every town (or " INF").
questions.constraints: 1 <= n <= 15; 0 <= m <= min(50, n(n-1)/2); 1 <= w <= 100; no self-loops or duplicate roads.
questions.easy: Dijkstra: repeatedly confirm the closest unfinished town, then relax its outgoing roads; unreachable towns print INF.
logic: dist[] starts at a huge value; dist[source] = 0.
Each round picks the unfinished town with the smallest finite distance, marks it done, and relaxes its neighbours.
dist[u] + graph[u][v] < dist[v] triggers the update.
Print " INF" for towns still at the huge value.
algorithm: dijkstra(n, source, dist): initialise; loop n times: pick u; if u == -1 break; done[u] = true; relax neighbours.
printDistances: "Distances:" then " dist[i]" or " INF" per town.
main: read graph and source; run; print.
mistakes: Selecting towns whose distance is still INFINITY as the minimum (guard with dist[v] != huge or break).
Relaxing with a road weight of 0 (0 means NO road in the matrix).
Printing INF as 1000000000 - the output must literally show INF.
questions.bugLabel: Relaxation treats 0 entries as roads (>= 0 instead of > 0), but 0 in the matrix means NO road - all distances collapse to wrong values.

questions.title: Minimum semesters (layered topological sort)
questions.statement: Dr. Fathima is the academic coordinator of a college that offers n courses numbered from 0 to n-1. Some courses have a prerequisite: "a b" means that the course a must be completed in an earlier semester before the course b can be taken. In every semester, a student takes all the courses whose prerequisites are already completed in the earlier semesters, and no other course. A course taken in a semester does not help the courses of the same semester. Write a program that prints the minimum number of semesters needed to complete all the courses. If the prerequisites contain a cycle, so that some course can never be taken, print a message.
questions.inputFormat: Line 1: integers n and m. Next m lines: a, b (a is a prerequisite of b).
questions.outputFormat: "Semesters: " + count, or "Impossible: Cycle in prerequisites".
questions.constraints: 1 <= n <= 15; 0 <= m <= min(50, n(n-1)); no self-loops or repeated prerequisites.
questions.easy: Layer-by-layer removal: every semester all courses with zero remaining prerequisites are taken together; if a round finds no such course, there is a cycle.
logic: Build the directed adjacency matrix and in-degrees.
Each round: collect ALL courses with indeg == 0 and not done (this is the semester batch).
Empty batch with courses left -> cycle -> print the Impossible message.
Mark the batch done, decrement each successor's indegree, semesters++.
algorithm: Read edges; set adj[a][b] = 1 and indeg[b]++ (guarding duplicates).
while taken < n: gather batch; if batch empty -> print Impossible and return.
For each u in batch: done[u] = true; taken++; for each j with adj[u][j] == 1: indeg[j]--.
semesters++; after the loop print "Semesters: " + semesters.
mistakes: Taking one course per semester instead of the whole zero-indegree batch (the sample expects 2, not 4).
Decrementing indegrees BEFORE printing... rather: updating batch members' indegrees within the same round must not enable same-semester chains (the batch is fixed first, then all decrements happen).
Missing the duplicate-edge guard (two identical prerequisites would double-decrement).

questions.title: Two debate teams (bipartite check with BFS colouring)
questions.statement: Ilango is a teacher who has to split n students numbered from 0 to n-1 into two debate teams, Team A and Team B. Some pairs of students are close friends, and he does not want two close friends to be in the same team, because they tend to agree on everything. Every student must be in exactly one team. Write a program that finds out whether such a split is possible. To make the answer unique, process the students from the smallest number to the largest. Every student who is not yet placed and is processed gets Team A, and the friends of a student placed in one team must be placed in the other team. Print the teams if the split is possible.
questions.inputFormat: Line 1: integers n and m. Next m lines: u, v (close friends).
questions.outputFormat: "Possible", then "Team A:" + numbers, then "Team B:" + numbers; or just "Not Possible".
questions.constraints: 1 <= n <= 15; 0 <= m <= min(50, n(n-1)/2); no self-loops or repeated pairs.
questions.easy: This is graph 2-colouring: BFS from every unplaced student (Team A = colour 0), give every friend the opposite colour, and fail when two friends already share a colour.
logic: color[i] = -1 means unplaced.
For each start in increasing order: if unplaced, colour it 0 and BFS.
Neighbour uncoloured -> colour 1 - color[u] and enqueue; neighbour with the SAME colour -> print Not Possible and stop.
Otherwise print Possible and list Team A (colour 0) and Team B (colour 1) in increasing order.
algorithm: Read edges into adj matrix; colour array init -1.
For start = 0..n-1: if color[start] != -1 continue; colour[start] = 0; BFS queue.
BFS loop: u = dequeue; for v = 0..n-1 with adj[u][v]: if color[v] == -1 -> colour and enqueue; else if color[v] == color[u] -> print Not Possible; return.
Print "Possible", then Team A / Team B loops.
mistakes: Processing components out of order - the answer must be unique, so always take the smallest unplaced student first.
Printing teams after detecting a conflict - return immediately.
Forgetting that the queue must hold vertices across the whole component, not just the start.

questions.title: Bellman-Ford cheapest route with negative-cycle detection
questions.statement: Gokul plans a long drive from the city 0 to the city n-1 through n cities numbered from 0 to n-1. Some one-way roads have a toll, which is a positive cost, and some roads give a rebate, which is a negative cost. If a driver can reach a group of roads that forms a loop with a negative total cost, the driver could earn unlimited rebates by driving around it, so the cheapest cost is not defined. Write a program that prints the minimum total cost of travelling from the city 0 to the city n-1. If the city n-1 cannot be reached from the city 0, print "No Route". If a loop with a negative total cost can be reached from the city 0, print "Negative Cycle" instead.
questions.inputFormat: Line 1: integers n and m. Next m lines: u, v, w (one-way road with cost w, w != 0).
questions.outputFormat: "Negative Cycle", "No Route", or "Minimum Cost: " + cost.
questions.constraints: 2 <= n <= 15; 0 <= m <= min(50, n(n-1)); -50 <= w <= 100, w != 0; no self-loops or repeated roads.
questions.easy: Bellman-Ford from city 0: relax every edge n-1 times; one extra relaxation pass detects negative cycles; then report the cost to city n-1.
logic: dist[0] = 0, everyone else infinity.
Repeat (n - 1) passes over ALL edges relaxing dist[v] = dist[u] + w when better.
One more pass: any further improvement reachable from 0 -> Negative Cycle.
dist[n-1] still infinity -> No Route; else print Minimum Cost.
algorithm: Store edges in arrays eu[], ev[], ew[].
for pass = 1..n-1: for each edge: relax if dist[u] finite and better.
for each edge: if still relaxable (from a finite dist) -> print Negative Cycle; return.
If dist[n-1] == INF print "No Route"; else print "Minimum Cost: " << dist[n-1].
mistakes: Running only one relaxation pass - negative edges need the full n-1 rounds to settle.
Detecting the cycle without checking reachability from city 0 (an unreachable negative loop must NOT trigger the message).
Reporting Minimum Cost when n-1 is unreachable.

questions.title: Connected components: count, largest size, connectivity
questions.statement: Hemalatha works for a telecom company that has built phone lines between the villages of a district. There are n villages numbered from 0 to n-1, and every phone line joins two villages and works in both directions. Two villages are in the same group if they can talk to each other, directly or through other villages. A village with no phone line forms a group alone. The network is called connected if all the villages are in one group. Write a program that prints the number of groups of villages, the number of villages in the largest group, and whether the network is connected.
questions.inputFormat: Line 1: integers n and m. Next m lines: u, v (a phone line).
questions.outputFormat: "Components: " + count; "Largest Component: " + size; "Connected: Yes/No".
questions.constraints: 1 <= n <= 15; 0 <= m <= min(50, n(n-1)/2); no self-loops or repeated lines.
questions.easy: DFS from every unvisited village; each new DFS start is one component; remember the size of the biggest component.
logic: dfs(u) marks u visited and returns 1 + sum of DFS sizes of unvisited neighbours.
Main loop: every unvisited vertex starts a new component; count++ and track largest.
components == 1 -> Connected: Yes.
algorithm: Read graph into adj matrix.
For i = 0..n-1: if not visited: size = dfs(i); components++; largest = max(largest, size).
Print Components / Largest Component / Connected lines.
mistakes: Counting a component per EDGE instead of per unvisited start vertex.
Forgetting isolated villages (m = 0) - each is its own component of size 1.
Comparing component size with largest using >= (ties must keep the FIRST largest - irrelevant for the value, but > is cleaner).

mcqs.q: What does polymorphism mean in OOP?
opts: Hiding the internal details of a class
Binding data with the functions that use it
The ability of the same interface to behave differently for different objects
mcqs.ansText: The ability of the same interface to behave differently for different objects
mcqs.expl: Poly = many, morph = forms: one function name or operator works in different ways for different objects (e.g., the same call show() prints different things for different classes).

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes procedural programming?
opts: A program is organized as a set of functions that operate on separate data
A program is organized as objects that combine data and functions
A program is written only using classes and inheritance
A program is written without using any functions
mcqs.ansText: A program is organized as a set of functions that operate on separate data
mcqs.expl: In procedural programming (like C), data and functions are separate; functions pass data around. OOP instead bundles data + functions together into objects.

mcqs.q: In a non-static member function, what does the this pointer hold?
opts: The address of the class definition
The address of the object that called the function
The address of the first data member only
The address of the base class
mcqs.ansText: The address of the object that called the function
mcqs.expl: this is automatically passed to every non-static member function and always points to the exact object used in the call, e.g. s.display() makes this point to s.

mcqs.q: Which OOP concept allows a new class to acquire the properties of an existing class?
mcqs.expl: A derived class automatically gets the data members and member functions of its base class, then can add or override its own.

mcqs.q: Which OOP concept binds data and the functions that operate on it into a single unit?
mcqs.expl: A class encapsulates data + the methods that use it in one unit and hides the data from outside - like a capsule.

mcqs.q: What is the default access specifier for members of a class in C++?
mcqs.expl: In a C++ class, members written before any access specifier are private. (Note the trap: for a struct the default is public - for a class it is private.)

mcqs.q: What is an object in C++?
opts: A blueprint that defines data members and member functions
A function that returns a value
mcqs.expl: The class is the blueprint; each variable created from it (e.g., Box b1;) is an object - a real instance occupying memory.

mcqs.q: Which operator is used to define a member function outside its class?
mcqs.expl: Outside definition uses the form  void Box::volume() { ... }  - the :: tells the compiler that volume belongs to class Box.

mcqs.q: Which keyword is used to define a class in C++?
mcqs.expl: Syntax: class Box { ... };  - note the semicolon after the closing brace (forgetting it is a classic compile error).

mcqs.q: Which C++ data type is used to store the values true and false?
mcqs.expl: bool holds only true (1) or false (0). Printing a bool with cout shows 1 or 0, not the words.

Same name and same parameters but different return types
Different names but the same parameters
Same name but defined in different files only

mcqs.q: In public inheritance, what do the public members of the base class become in the derived class?

mcqs.q: Which type of inheritance has a class derived from two or more base classes?

mcqs.q: Where can a protected member of a base class be accessed?
opts: Within the base class and its derived classes
mcqs.ansText: Within the base class and its derived classes
mcqs.expl: protected behaves like private for the outside world, but derived classes can use it directly (e.g., brand and storage in the Device/Phone program).

mcqs.q: Which operator cannot be overloaded in C++?
mcqs.expl: :: , . (dot), .* and sizeof can never be overloaded. + , << and [] are commonly overloaded (Complex +, cout <<, array subscript).

mcqs.q: Which keyword makes a base class member function eligible for dynamic binding?
mcqs.expl: Declaring the base function virtual lets the call be resolved at run time based on the actual object type (needed for Employee* ->salary() in the salary program).

mcqs.q: What is method overriding?
opts: A derived class giving its own definition of a base class function with the same signature
Defining two functions with the same name and different parameters
Calling a base class constructor from main()
Hiding all members of the base class
mcqs.ansText: A derived class giving its own definition of a base class function with the same signature
mcqs.expl: Same name, same parameters, but the derived version replaces the base version (B is overloading, not overriding).

mcqs.q: Which statement about the this pointer is correct?
opts: It is a static member of every class
It stores the address of the base class
It can be used inside static member functions
It is passed implicitly to every non-static member function
mcqs.ansText: It is passed implicitly to every non-static member function
mcqs.expl: Every non-static member function receives this automatically. Static member functions have no this because they belong to the class, not an object (C is a classic trap).

mcqs.q: In what order are constructors called when a derived class object is created?
opts: Derived class first, then base class
Only the derived class constructor is called
Base class first, then derived class
mcqs.ansText: Base class first, then derived class
mcqs.expl: The base part must exist before the derived part builds on it. Destructors run in exactly the reverse order (derived first).

mcqs.q: A class becomes abstract in C++ when it contains at least one:

mcqs.q: What is a concrete class?

A class that implements all its functions and can be instantiated
A class that cannot have any objects
A class that has only static members

mcqs.expl: Concrete = the opposite of abstract: every pure virtual function is implemented, so objects can be created (CardPayment and UpiPayment in the Payment program).

mcqs.q: When is the function to be called decided in dynamic binding?
mcqs.expl: With virtual functions through a base pointer, the actual function is chosen while the program runs, using the real object type.

opts: Data and a pointer to the next node
Data and pointers to the previous and next nodes
Only a pointer to the head

mcqs.expl: A singly linked node stores its data plus one link to the following node (B describes a doubly linked list node).

mcqs.q: Which order does a queue follow for insertion and removal?
mcqs.expl: The first element inserted is removed first, like a line of people. LIFO is a stack.

mcqs.q: Which extra pointer does a node of a doubly linked list have compared with a singly linked list node?
opts: A pointer to the middle node
A pointer to the previous node
A pointer to the data type
mcqs.ansText: A pointer to the previous node
mcqs.expl: Doubly linked nodes keep prev AND next, so traversal works in both directions (see the recent-files program).

mcqs.q: In a circular singly linked list, where does the next pointer of the last node point?
mcqs.expl: The last node links back to the head, forming a ring (that is why the walk-around program can loop using while (temp->next != head)).

mcqs.q: What is the time complexity of inserting a node at the beginning of a singly linked list when the head pointer is available?
mcqs.expl: Only a few pointer assignments are needed - no traversal - so it is constant time. Inserting at the END without a tail pointer is O(n) (must walk the whole list).

mcqs.q: In a linked list implementation of a queue, where is a new element inserted?
opts: At a position chosen by its value
mcqs.expl: Queues are FIFO: insert at the rear, remove from the front. Keeping both a front and a rear pointer makes both operations O(1).

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an application of a queue?
mcqs.expl: Waiting processes are served in arrival order -> a queue. B, C and D are STACK applications (last in, first out).

mcqs.q: In a priority queue, which element is removed first?
opts: The element with the highest priority
mcqs.ansText: The element with the highest priority
mcqs.expl: Priority queues serve by importance, not by age (in a min-heap the smallest number = most urgent is served first).

mcqs.q: Which stack operation adds an element to the top of the stack?
mcqs.expl: push adds on top, pop removes from the top, peek only looks at the top, enqueue belongs to queues.

mcqs.q: Which problem of a simple array-based queue is solved by a circular queue?
opts: Wasted space at the front after dequeues
mcqs.ansText: Wasted space at the front after dequeues
mcqs.expl: In a linear array the freed front cells can never be reused, so the array fills up early. The circular queue reuses them with the modulo trick rear = (rear + 1) % capacity.

mcqs.q: What is the postfix form of the infix expression A * B + C?
mcqs.expl: * has higher precedence than +, so A B * is done first, then + C: the operators are written right after their operands.

mcqs.q: While evaluating a postfix expression with a stack, what is done when an operator is encountered?

It is added to the output string
Two operands are popped, the operation is applied and the result is pushed

mcqs.expl: Operands are pushed; when an operator arrives, pop b then pop a (order matters for - and /), compute a op b, push the result back.

mcqs.q: In infix to postfix conversion, what is done when a closing parenthesis is encountered?

Operators are popped to the output until the matching opening parenthesis is reached
All operands are popped from the stack
mcqs.ansText: Operators are popped to the output until the matching opening parenthesis is reached
mcqs.expl: Both the closing and the opening parenthesis are then discarded - they never appear in the postfix output.

mcqs.q: Which property holds for every node of a binary search tree?
opts: Keys in the left sub tree are smaller and keys in the right sub tree are larger
Keys in the left sub tree are larger and keys in the right sub tree are smaller
Both sub tree always have the same height
All keys in the tree are equal

mcqs.q: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in ascending order?

mcqs.q: What is the maximum number of children a node can have in a binary tree?
mcqs.expl: Binary = at most two children (left and right). A node may have 0, 1 or 2 children.

mcqs.q: If the root is at height 0, what is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h?
mcqs.expl: Level i can hold 2^i nodes; levels 0..h sum to 1 + 2 + 4 + ... + 2^h = 2^(h+1) - 1. Example: height 2 -> up to 7 nodes.

mcqs.q: A tree with n nodes has how many edges?
mcqs.expl: Every node except the root has exactly one incoming edge, so n nodes give n - 1 edges.

mcqs.q: Which operations are used to restore the red-black properties after an insertion?
mcqs.expl: After inserting a red node, the tree fixes red-red conflicts by recolouring and, when needed, rotating - never by deleting or re-sorting.

mcqs.q: Which property is true for a red-black tree?
opts: A red node cannot have a red child
mcqs.ansText: A red node cannot have a red child
mcqs.expl: The red rule forbids two consecutive red nodes on a path. The root is always BLACK (B is a trap), and leaves are considered black.

mcqs.q: What do the internal nodes of an expression tree contain?
mcqs.expl: Leaves hold operands (numbers/variables); internal nodes hold the operators (+, -, *, /) that combine their subtrees.

mcqs.q: What is the colour of the root node in a red-black tree?
mcqs.expl: The root must be black - this is checked explicitly in the red-black colouring program (color[0] == 'R' means invalid).

mcqs.q: Where is the largest key located in a binary search tree?
mcqs.expl: Keep going right from the root until there is no right child (findMax walks temp->right). The leftmost node holds the minimum.

mcqs.q: Which rotation corrects the Left-Right (LR) imbalance in an AVL tree?
opts: Right rotation followed by left rotation
Left rotation followed by right rotation
mcqs.ansText: Left rotation followed by right rotation
mcqs.expl: LR case: the left child leans right, so first rotate LEFT around the left child, then rotate RIGHT around the root. (C describes the RL case - read the letters carefully.)

mcqs.q: Which balance factor values are allowed for every node of an AVL tree?
mcqs.expl: Balance factor = height(left) - height(right) must stay in {-1, 0, +1}. If it becomes ±2, a rotation is required immediately.

mcqs.q: In which kind of graph does BFS give the shortest path in terms of the number of edges?
mcqs.expl: BFS explores layer by layer, so the first time it reaches a vertex is via the fewest edges - true whenever all edges count equally (unweighted).

mcqs.q: Which data structure does breadth-first search use?
mcqs.expl: BFS keeps a FIFO queue of discovered vertices. DFS uses a stack (explicitly or via recursion).

mcqs.q: What is true about the adjacency matrix of an undirected graph?
opts: It is always a diagonal matrix
mcqs.expl: An undirected edge i-j sets BOTH adj[i][j] and adj[j][i] to 1, so the matrix mirrors across its diagonal (that is why addEdge sets both).

mcqs.q: Which approach produces a topological ordering of a DAG?
opts: Repeatedly removing a vertex with in-degree zero
Repeatedly removing the vertex of maximum degree
Visiting edges in decreasing order of weight
mcqs.ansText: Repeatedly removing a vertex with in-degree zero
mcqs.expl: Kahn's algorithm: take any vertex with no incoming edges left, output it, delete its outgoing edges, repeat. This is also the basis of the 'minimum semesters' program.

mcqs.q: Which data structure does an iterative depth first search use?
mcqs.expl: DFS goes deep first and backtracks - exactly LIFO behaviour (recursion uses the call stack automatically).

mcqs.q: What is the space complexity of the adjacency matrix representation of a graph with V vertices?
mcqs.expl: A V x V matrix stores V² cells whether or not edges exist - fine for small V (like the 15-vertex problems here), wasteful for large sparse graphs.

mcqs.q: A topological ordering exists only for which kind of graph?
mcqs.expl: A cycle means every vertex in it always has an in-degree > 0, so no valid order exists - the 'Impossible: Cycle in prerequisites' output.

mcqs.q: What is the space complexity of the adjacency list representation of a graph with V vertices and E edges?
mcqs.expl: One list per vertex plus one entry per edge - much better than O(V²) when the graph is sparse (few edges).

mcqs.q: Dijkstra's algorithm does not give correct results for graphs containing which kind of edges?
mcqs.expl: Dijkstra marks a vertex 'done' too early, so a later negative edge can no longer improve it - use Bellman-Ford when negative edges exist.

mcqs.q: How does Prim's algorithm grow a minimum spanning tree?
opts: By adding the heaviest edge that connects the tree to a new vertex
By adding the minimum-weight edge that connects the tree to a new vertex
By visiting vertices in depth first order
mcqs.ansText: By adding the minimum-weight edge that connects the tree to a new vertex
mcqs.expl: At every step Prim takes the cheapest edge crossing from the tree built so far to an outside vertex (key[v] update in the MST program).

mcqs.q: When is an undirected graph said to be connected?
opts: There is a path between every pair of vertices
mcqs.ansText: There is a path between every pair of vertices
mcqs.expl: All vertices must be in one component. The components program counts groups by running DFS from every unvisited vertex.

mcqs.q: How many edges does a minimum spanning tree of a connected graph with V vertices have?
mcqs.expl: A spanning tree connects all V vertices with exactly V - 1 edges - any more would create a cycle.
